meta.summary: Initial tracker seeded from the July 29, 2026 public thread about practical open replacements for closed personal infrastructure.
verificationRules: Use official repositories, project sites, or original public posts before naming a builder or maintainer.
Keep signal sources separate from builders and maintainers.
Mark a project as verification pending when the project exists but the thread-to-project mapping is not proved.
Do not infer personal attribution from repository popularity, reposts, or commentary.

projects.name: FreeFlow
projects.replacesOrEnables: A free and inspectable alternative to closed voice-dictation tools such as Wispr Flow, Superwhisper, and Monologue.

evidence.label: GitHub repository
evidence.note: Repository description identifies FreeFlow as a free and fast alternative to Wispr Flow; GitHub reports the repo as active and MIT licensed.

evidence.label: README attribution
evidence.note: README credits Marc Bodea for maintaining FreeFlow.

people.name: Zach Latta
people.evidence: Official repository and project site are under Zach Latta's public namespace.

people.name: Marc Bodea
people.evidence: FreeFlow README explicitly thanks Marc Bodea for maintaining the project.

projects.name: Quill + Quill CLI
projects.focusArea: Private meeting capture and local transcript access
projects.replacesOrEnables: A Granola-like meeting-notes workflow with a verified open-source CLI for local Quill data access.

evidence.label: Official site
evidence.note: Quill describes private meeting recording and transcription without bots.

evidence.label: CLI repository
evidence.note: GitHub reports quill-cli as an active MIT-licensed repository owned by Quill Meetings.

people.name: Quill Meetings
people.evidence: The verified open-source CLI is published under the Quill Meetings GitHub organization.

projects.notes: The verified open-source artifact is the CLI. This tracker does not claim that the full desktop app is open source.

signals.name: Andrew
signals.note: Surfaced Quill in the quoted July 29 thread. This is a signal role, not a maintainer attribution.

signals.name: Pieter Levels
signals.note: Commented on the broader pattern of closed products being reimplemented. This is a signal role, not a builder attribution for the listed projects.

leads.name: OpenStrap Edge
leads.replacesOrEnables: Makes a WHOOP 4.0 band useful without a WHOOP subscription by pairing over Bluetooth and computing metrics on the phone.

evidence.label: GitHub repository
evidence.note: Repository description identifies a WHOOP 4.0 app that works without a WHOOP subscription; GitHub reports the repo as active and MIT licensed.

people.name: OpenStrap
people.evidence: The repository is published and maintained under the OpenStrap GitHub organization.

leads.pendingReason: Verified as an active WHOOP project, but not verified as the exact project Pieter Levels referenced.

leads.name: Goose
leads.replacesOrEnables: A local-first experiment for reading WHOOP 5.0 BLE data.

evidence.label: GitHub repository
evidence.note: GitHub reports the repository as archived; README describes it as an alpha proof of concept.

people.name: Bennett
people.evidence: The repository is published under the b-nnett GitHub account.

leads.pendingReason: The project is real, but it is not verified as the exact WHOOP project referenced by Pieter Levels.

leads.name: Wearable / my-whoop
leads.replacesOrEnables: A small experimental repository for extracting data from a WHOOP wearable.

evidence.label: GitHub repository
evidence.note: GitHub reports an active public repository, but no license and no project site were found during initial verification.

people.name: John Middleton
people.evidence: The repository is published under the johnmiddleton12 GitHub account.

leads.pendingReason: Retained as a WHOOP source lead because the exact Levels-referenced project was not uniquely identified.
